ai.description: This 4–5 cm skink is bronze-brown with a distinct dark lateral stripe. It features fused eyelids, a streamlined body, and reduced limbs with five digits. It lacks a visible external ear opening.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ablepharus ladacensis* is best distinguished by its fused, immovable eyelids that form a transparent spectacle, unlike the movable, scaly eyelids found in most other skinks.
ai.habitat: The Ladak Ground Skink inhabits high-altitude, arid alpine meadows and rocky slopes in the Himalayas, typically ranging between 3,000 and 4,500 meters above sea level.
ai.behavior: The Ladak Ground Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among rocky crevices and alpine scree slopes during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ablepharus ladacensis* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–3 eggs during the summer breeding season (June to August) in high-altitude regions of India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Ladak Ground Skink occurs across the high-altitude regions of Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh, typically inhabiting arid, rocky terrain between 3,000 and 4,500 meters.
